paper.instructions:
(i) This question paper contains 33 questions. All questions are compulsory.
(ii) This question paper is divided into five sections – Section A, B, C, D and E.
(iii) Section A – questions number 1 to 16 are multiple choice type questions. Each question carries 1 mark.
(iv) Section B – questions number 17 to 21 are very short answer type questions. Each question carries 2 marks.
(v) Section C – questions number 22 to 28 are short answer type questions. Each question carries 3 marks.
(vi) Section D – questions number 29 and 30 are case-based questions. Each question carries 4 marks.
(vii) Section E – questions number 31 to 33 are long answer type questions. Each question carries 5 marks.
(viii) There is no overall choice given in the question paper. However, an internal choice has been provided in few questions in all the sections except Section –A.
(ix) Kindly note that there is a separate question paper for Visually Impaired candidates.
(x) Use of calculator is NOT allowed.

questions.stem:
What type of deviation from Raoult's law is shown by a mixture of phenol and aniline ? Give reason.
What will happen to the boiling point of the solution on mixing phenol and aniline ?
questions.solution:
Negative deviation (½)
Solute-solvent interactions are stronger than solute-solute and solvent-solvent. / The intermolecular hydrogen bonding between phenolic proton and lone pair on nitrogen atom of aniline is stronger than the respective intermolecular hydrogen bonding between similar molecules (1)
Boiling point of the solution increases. (½)

questions.stem: Why are haloarenes less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reaction ? Give two reasons.
questions.solution:
Because of, (Any two) (1 + 1)
(i) $\mathrm{C-X}$ acquires partial double bond due to resonance
(ii) $sp^{2}$ hybridization of C of $\mathrm{C-X}$ make it more electronegative and hold the electron pair tightly.
(iii) repulsion between nucleophile and electron rich arenes.
(iv) Instability of phenyl cation

Differentiate between the following : (2 × 1)
(i) Peptide linkage and Glycosidic linkage
(ii) Essential amino acids and Non-essential amino acids
questions.solution:
(i) It is an amide linkage formed between two amino acids through $\mathrm{-CONH-}$ / an amide linkage formed between $\mathrm{-COOH}$ and $\mathrm{-NH_2}$ group whereas in glycosidic linkage two or more monosaccharides are joined together by an oxygen atom. (1)

questions.stem:
Following reaction takes place in one step :
$$\mathrm{2A + B \longrightarrow 2C}$$
How will the rate of above reaction change if the volume of the reaction vessel is decreased to one third of its original volume ? Will there be any change in the order of reaction with the reduced volume ?
questions.solution:
$\text{Rate} = k[\mathrm{A}]^{2}[\mathrm{B}]$
If the volume is decreased to $\frac{1}{3}$rd of original concentration increases 3 times
$\therefore \text{Rate} = k[3\mathrm{A}]^{2}[3\mathrm{B}] = 27\,k[\mathrm{A}]^{2}[\mathrm{B}]$
Hence rate will be increased by 27 times. (1)
Order remains same. (1)

questions.stem: Calculate the boiling point of a solution containing 0.61 g of benzoic acid (Molar mass = $122\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$) in 5 g of $\mathrm{CS_2}$ in which it dimerises to the extent of 88%. The boiling point and $K_b$ of $\mathrm{CS_2}$ are $46.2\ ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $2.3\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$ respectively.
questions.solution:
$\alpha = 88\% = 0.88$
$\Delta T_b = i K_b m = i K_b \frac{W_B}{M_B} \times \frac{1000}{W_A}$ (½)
$0.88 = \frac{1 - i}{1 - \frac{1}{2}}$
$i = 0.56$ (½)
$T_b - T_b^{\circ} = 0.56 \times 2.3 \times \frac{0.61}{122} \times \frac{1000}{5}$
$T_b - 46.2\ ^{\circ}\mathrm{C} = 1.288\ \mathrm{K}$ or $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (1)
$\therefore T_b = (46.2 + 1.288)\ ^{\circ}\mathrm{C} = 47.488\ ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ / $320.638\ \mathrm{K}$ (1)

(b) Due to the strong electron withdrawing effect of the carbonyl group / resonance stabilisation of their conjugate base. (1)
(c) Protonation of nucleophile takes place in strongly acidic medium. (1)

questions.stem:
Compound 'X' with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_4H_9Br}$ reacts with aqueous KOH to give an alcohol. The rate of this reaction depends only on the concentration of the compound 'X'. When an optically active isomer 'Y' of the compound 'X' was treated with aqueous KOH solution, the rate of reaction was found to be dependent on concentration of compound 'Y' and aqueous KOH both. (3 × 1)
(a) Write down the structural formula of both 'X' and 'Y'.
(b) Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will undergo racemisation and why ?
(c) Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will form product with inversion of configuration and why ?
questions.solution:
(a) X = $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-Br}$ ; Y = $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_2-CH_3}$ (see figure) (½ + ½)
(b) X, because reaction is $\mathrm{S_N1}$ / due to formation of planar carbocation as intermediate. (½ + ½)
(Full marks are also awarded if the student writes Y, which is optically active.)
(c) Y, Because reaction is $\mathrm{S_N2}$ / due to rear side attack of nucleophile. (½ + ½)

questions.stem:
The reaction of amines with mineral acids to form ammonium salts shows that these are basic in nature. Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia whereas aromatic amines are weaker bases than ammonia. Aliphatic and aromatic primary and secondary amines react with acid chlorides, anhydrides and esters by nucleophilic substitution reaction. The main problem encountered during electrophilic substitution reactions of aromatic amines is that of their high reactivity. Substitution tends to occur at ortho-and para-positions. Hinsberg reagent is used for the identification and distinction between primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Aryldiazonium salts, usually obtained from arylamines, undergo replacement of the diazonium group with a variety of nucleophiles to provide advantageous methods for producing aryl halides, cyanides, phenols and arenes.

Answer the following questions :
(a) (i) Why $\mathrm{CH_3-NH_2}$ is a stronger base than $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3N}$ in aqueous solution ? (2 × 1)
(ii) Write structural formulae of the compound A and B :
$\mathrm{CH_3CONH_2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaOBr}} \mathrm{A} \xrightarrow[\text{Base}]{\mathrm{C_6H_5COC}l} \mathrm{B}$
(b) A compound 'X' with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_3H_9N}$ reacts with Hinsberg reagent to give a product insoluble in alkali. Identify 'X'. (1)
OR
(b) How can you convert aniline to benzonitrile ? (1)
(c) Why is $\mathrm{-NH_2}$ group of aniline acetylated before carrying out nitration ? (1)
questions.solution:
(a) (i) Due to combined effect of the inductive effect, solvation effect and steric hinderance of the alkyl group. (1)
(ii) A = $\mathrm{CH_3NH_2}$, B = $\mathrm{CH_3{-}NHCOC_6H_5}$ (½ + ½)
(b) $\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}NH{-}CH_3}$ / N – Methylethanamine (1)
OR
(b) $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2} \xrightarrow[0-5\ {}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}]{\mathrm{NaNO_2 + HCl}} \mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^{+}Cl^{-}} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{CuCN}} \mathrm{C_6H_5CN}$ (1)
(c) The nitration reaction can be controlled and the p-nitro derivative can be obtained as the major product / To prevent the formation of anilinium ion which is meta directing. (1)

questions.stem:
The Valence Bond Theory (VBT) explains the formation, magnetic behaviour and geometry of coordination compounds. The Crystal Field Theory (CFT) of coordination compounds is based on the effect of different crystal fields (provided by the ligands taken as point charges), on the degeneracy of d-orbital energies of the central metal atom/ion. The splitting of the d-orbitals provides different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields.

Answer the following questions :
(a) In octahedral crystal field, energies of which d-orbitals will be raised when ligands approach the central metal atom/ion ? Give reason in support of your answer. (2)
(b) Using crystal field theory, write the electronic configuration of central metal atom/ion of the following : (1)
(i) $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$
(ii) $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ [At. No. : Co = 27]
(c) $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$ is paramagnetic while $\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}$ is diamagnetic though both are tetrahedral. Why ? [Atomic No. : Ni = 28] (1)
OR
(c) Write hybridization and magnetic behaviour of the complex $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}$. [Atomic No. : Fe = 26] (1)
questions.solution:
(a) $d_{x^{2}-y^{2}}$ and $d_{z^{2}}$ (1)
In Octahedral Crystal field, ligands approach metal atom/ion along the axis due to which $d_{x^{2}-y^{2}}$ and $d_{z^{2}}$ orbitals experience more repulsion. (1)
(b) (i) $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$ : $\mathrm{Co^{3+}} = 3d^{6}$, $t_{2g}^{4}\,e_{g}^{2}$ (½)
(ii) $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ : $\mathrm{Co^{3+}} = 3d^{6}$, $t_{2g}^{6}\,e_{g}^{0}$ (½)
(c) In $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{Cl^{-}}$ is a weak field ligand and does not pair up the unpaired electrons in 3d-orbital and hence paramagnetic. (½)
In $\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}$, CO being a strong field ligand pair up the unpaired electrons and hence diamagnetic. (½)
OR
(c) Hybridisation – $d^{2}sp^{3}$
Magnetic behaviour : Paramagnetic (½ + ½)

questions.stem:
(i) From the given data of $E^{\circ}$ values, answer the following questions : (3 + 2)
 | V | Cr | Mn | Fe | Co | Ni | Cu
$E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{M^{2+}/M}}$ | $-1.18$ | $-0.91$ | $-1.18$ | $-0.44$ | $-0.28$ | $-0.25$ | $+0.34$
(I) Why $E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{M^{2+}/M}}$ show irregular trend in the above values ?
(II) Why is $E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Cu^{2+}/Cu}}$ value exceptionally positive ?
(III) Why $E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Mn^{2+}/Mn}}$ value is highly negative ?
(ii) Write the ionic equations for the oxidising action of potassium permanganate for its reaction with $\mathrm{I^{-}}$ in both acidic and alkaline solutions.
questions.solution:
(i) (I) Due to the irregular variation of ionisation enthalpies ($\Delta_{i}H_{1} + \Delta_{i}H_{2}$) and sublimation enthalpies. (1)
(II) Due to low $\Delta_{hyd}H^{\circ}$ and high $\Delta_{a}H^{\circ}$ of Cu. (1)
(III) Because $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ is highly stable due to half-filled $3d^{5}$ configuration. (1)
(ii) $\mathrm{2MnO_4^{-} + 10I^{-} + 16H^{+} \rightarrow 2Mn^{2+} + 8H_2O + 5I_2}$ (1)
$\mathrm{2MnO_4^{-} + I^{-} + H_2O \rightarrow 2MnO_2 + IO_3^{-} + 2OH^{-}}$ (1)
